claims.text: Preheating the build chamber during laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi reduces thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients decrease residual stresses in laser-powder-bed-fused AlCrFeNiSi.
Build-chamber preheating refines the microstructure of laser-powder-bed-fused AlCrFeNiSi.
The resulting microstructural refinement improves mechanical properties relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The feedstock is gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi powder with a particle-size distribution typical of additive manufacturing.
The proposed intervention is to preheat the laser powder bed fusion build chamber to approximately 600°C.
Miniature AlCrFeNiSi components are to be fabricated in an argon atmosphere with laser power and scan speed optimized for controlled energy input.
Preheating produces a more uniform microstructure with fewer internal dislocations.
Preheating mitigates the thermal shock and rapid cooling associated with conventional laser powder bed fusion.
Mitigating thermal shock and rapid cooling lowers the rate of solidification-induced stress buildup.
Build-chamber preheating promotes a more homogeneous grain structure.
A more homogeneous grain structure enhances ductility and overall mechanical performance.
Components produced with approximately 600°C preheating will have significantly lower residual thermal stresses than components built at ambient chamber temperature.
Components produced with approximately 600°C preheating will have greater ductility and toughness than components built at ambient chamber temperature.
Conventional ambient-temperature laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi typically creates high thermal gradients and residual-stress accumulation.
Residual-stress accumulation under conventional processing degrades the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components.
The proposed effective build-chamber preheating window is approximately 500–700°C for miniature components made with comparable energy input and scanning strategies.
The optimum preheat temperature may depend on machine-specific parameters and powder characteristics.
